the mortality and morbidity of acute stage patients with cerebral hemorrhage, who were treated conservatively with intensive care, are not so high as those of the past.

, in the treatment of acute stage, the patients should be transported to the hospital as early as possible, preferably by hospital ambulance, and that patients with disturbed consciousness should be treated in the NCU, or sub-NCU, and that patients should not be given intracranial pressure reducing agents or anticoagulants in acute stage.

conservative treatment of acute cerebral hemorrhage is effective in the prevention of complications and the reduction of mortality and morbidity, provided the patients are transported to the hospital as early as possible and are treated in NCUs or sub-NCU.
